explainers.rev:
Where this comes from

Money coming in

Confirmed customer orders, added up by the month they were placed.

The last full month is the latest calendar month the records cover to its final day; the best month is the strongest month on record.
How it is put together
Where it is kept
ERPNext, under customer orders
What counts
Only confirmed orders. Anything still a draft is left out.
How it is worked out
Every order's value, grouped by the month it was placed
What it excludes
Cancelled orders, and invoices never issued
How fresh
What changed in ERPNext is read every two minutes, and open screens refresh themselves every minute; the screen says when it was last loaded
explainers.ar:
Where this comes from

Money owed to us

Customer Ledger Balance, and its age.

The cards give the total and the invoices behind it; the panels show who owes the most, how long it has been, and why the invoices say otherwise.
How it is put together
Where it is kept
General Ledger, by Customer
How it is worked out
Each Customer Ledger Balance: everything debited to the customer less everything credited. A customer who owes nothing or is in credit adds nothing; customers in credit are counted separately.
Why Not Invoice Outstanding
Where a payment is never matched to the invoice it pays, the invoice still shows as unpaid though the money is in. The open invoices' own total is shown beside the Customer Ledger's, with the reason for the difference.
How the ages are set
Payments and credits not matched to an invoice are set against the customer's oldest invoices and opening balances first, the usual assumption when payments are not matched; what is left is aged from its due date to the latest date the records cover
Unpaid invoices
A count of the invoices still open on their own terms, and what they say is owed
Checked against
The business's ERPNext, line by line, under Settings, Businesses, Check Figures
explainers.ledger:
Where this comes from

What each really owes

Each Customer and Supplier Ledger Balance, beside Invoice Outstanding.

Each name opens its General Ledger.
How it is put together
Invoice Outstanding
What the invoices themselves still show as unpaid
Party Ledger Balance
General Ledger balance: a customer's debits less credits, a supplier's credits less debits. Negative means in credit.
Difference and why
Payments received or made but never matched to an invoice; payments and credit notes recorded against invoices that still show them unpaid; journal entries and credit notes not linked to an invoice; less amounts owed on no invoice at all, such as opening balances. When the records do not account for all of it, the remainder is said plainly.
The ages
After the unmatched payments and credits are set against the oldest open items first
Putting it right
Reconcile them in Accounts, Payment Reconciliation. Outstanding Amounts then agree with the Ledger Balance.

explainers.cover:
Where this comes from

Promised orders and what covers them

Every order line still to deliver, with the stock or purchase that will fill it.

Each row opens the order line, its stock and its purchase chain, with links to the documents in ERPNext.
How it is put together
Where it is kept
ERPNext: the open sales orders, the stock in each warehouse, and the purchase orders, material requests, goods receipts and supplier invoices
What counts
Confirmed orders not completed or closed, line by line, with quantity still to deliver
Linked
A purchase order or material request raised from the sales order (Create, Purchase Order or Material Request) names the order it is for, and is followed to the goods receipt and the supplier invoice
Likely
Where nothing names the order: an open purchase order for the same item, raised shortly before or after the order and linked to no other order. Each is counted once, oldest promise first, with the reason given
Stock
What the line's own warehouse holds, then any other warehouse goods are sold from, shared out oldest promise first so that no unit is counted twice
The states
In Stock, Received, On Order, Requested, Partly Covered, Not Ordered, Not a Stock Item. Late to Customer when the delivery date has passed; Supplier Late when the purchase order is past the date asked for
The settings
How far before and after an order a purchase order may be raised and still count as likely: Settings, Recommendations, Promised to customers, not ordered
explainers.drafts:
